title: How Browsers Parse, Render, and Execute a Page
description: Connect HTML parsing, DOM/CSSOM, style, layout, paint and script loading with browser performance.
learningOutcomes: Describe the simplified critical rendering path.
Distinguish DOM, CSSOM, layout, paint and compositing.
Explain how async/defer affects parsing and script order.
Recognize layout thrashing and long tasks.
Use DevTools to analyze a slow page.

blocks.text: A browser turns resources into an interactive page

A browser coordinates networking, caches, document parsing, style calculation, layout, painting, JavaScript, input, accessibility and security. Modern browsers use different processes and threads, so the pipeline below is a debugging model, not a rigid specification for every engine.

blocks.title: Think about the critical path
blocks.text: Content appears when the required resources and computations are ready. Large stylesheets, blocking scripts, images, fonts, long JavaScript tasks and expensive layout can delay a page. Measure the actual bottleneck first.

items: HTML parsing: bytes become tokens and nodes, building the DOM.
CSS processing: CSS becomes CSSOM/style data and applicable rules are determined.
Style calculation: computed styles and rendering data are produced.
Layout: positions and sizes are calculated.
Paint/rasterization: drawing commands and pixels/layers are produced.
Compositing: layers are combined for a display frame; GPU work is not free.

blocks.code:
HTML bytes → DOM
CSS resources → CSSOM
Compute applicable styles
Layout: positions and sizes
Paint / rasterize pixels
Composite layers → frame

steps.title: Parse HTML
steps.explanation: The parser builds a node tree; streaming parsing can start before loading finishes.

steps.title: Compute styles and geometry
steps.explanation: CSSOM contains parsed rules; the browser then computes styles and element geometry.

steps.title: Prepare and show the frame
steps.explanation: Painting and compositing prepare visual output. Engines optimize these steps differently.

blocks.text: DOM and CSSOM are different models

The DOM describes document structure; CSSOM describes parsed CSS rules and style data. JavaScript can change DOM/styles and trigger recalculation. A DOM change does not necessarily change pixels: a hidden element is not rendered like visible content.

A classic script without async/defer can pause HTML parsing while fetched/executed. defer downloads in parallel and runs after parsing while preserving classic-script order. async runs when ready without guaranteeing order. Modules are deferred by default. These attributes affect ordering, but do not guarantee code correctness or performance.

blocks.caption: Script attribute examples
blocks.code:
<script src="legacy.js"></script>
<script defer src="app.js"></script>
<script async src="metrics.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="main.js"></script>

blocks.text: Long synchronous JavaScript delays input and UI updates. Geometry changes may require layout and paint; other changes may require only paint. Layout thrashing occurs when code repeatedly writes styles then immediately reads geometry such as offsetHeight. Use Performance traces to find the cost rather than guessing.

blocks.title: Browser architecture and security
blocks.text: Browser/UI, network and renderer processes vary by engine. Sandboxing limits renderer access and the same-origin policy constrains documents from different origins. These are layers of defense, not a guarantee that every API or data source is safe.

options.feedback: These are the key simplified stages from markup to frame.

options.text: Paint first, then HTML and DOM
options.feedback: The browser must parse content and compute geometry before painting it.
Networking, parsing and scripts can overlap.

blocks.prompt: What is the main difference between defer and async for classic external scripts?

options.text: defer runs after parsing and preserves order; async runs when ready without guaranteeing order
options.feedback: defer preserves document order after parsing; async runs when available.

options.text: They are identical and only change CSS
options.feedback: They change how script fetching/execution relates to parsing.

blocks.explanation: Choose based on dependencies and required execution order.
